title: Ultimate 10-Point Job Search Checklist to Fast Track Success (2024)
description:
If you feel like the job search process is overwhelming, don’t worry; you’re not alone. With so many steps to keep track of, it's easy to feel lost. 

But having a comprehensive job search checklist can remove a lot of anxiety from the process and help you stay motivated.

The job search process contains several key steps you'll need to navigate. Generally, it includes:

• Researching job titles, companies, and industries you're interested in
• Updating your resume and cover letters
• Building your professional network through networking events and updating your LinkedIn profile
• Identifying and applying to job postings
• Preparing for and attending interviews
• Evaluating any offers and negotiating if needed

Having a clear job search plan for each of these stages is critical for an effective job search. Without direction, it’s easy to feel overwhelmed by the process. But mapping out goals for each phase will help you stay focused and maximize your chances of success.

title: How to Write Your Resume & Cover Letter with Google Gemini
description:
Are you struggling to create personalized resumes during your job search and considering Google's Gemini to help you out? 

In this video, you'll learn how to use Gemini to create the following:

1 Professional summary

How to do it: 

1. Copy/paste your resume (from the Teal Resume Builder or an existing resume) into Gemini.
2. Prompt: "Write a professional summary based on my resume and keep it under 100 words."
3. Copy/paste the output back into your resume and adjust as needed. 

2 Resume bullet point achievements

How to do it: 

1. Head to your Teal Job Tracker, and copy/paste the responsibilities section of a job description you're interested in.
2. Prompt: "Write 5 resume achievements with metrics based on these job responsibilities."
3. Make sure the metrics are accurate—you don't want to lie on your resume! Tweak the results as needed before you copy/paste back into your resume.

3 Skills (Based off the job description)

How to do it:

1. Prompt: "What relevant skills should I include in my resume for the position of [insert job title]? Here is a description of the role:"
2. Head to your Teal Job Tracker and copy the job description below the Gemini prompt.
3. Swap out the placeholder [JOB TITLE] with the title of the job you're applying to.
4. All the list of the skills to your resume skills section and anywhere else they apply across your resume.

4 Cover letter

How to do it: 

1. Copy/paste your resume from the Teal Resume Builder, along with the job description you're interested in.
2. Prompt: "Write a cover letter using my resume and a job description."
3. Copy/paste the results into a Word doc, Google doc, email, or the notes section of the saved jobs in your Teal Job Tracker.

 Note: You'll want to edit these after AI takes the first pass. The tech is there to help and support you, but we don't encourage using it as a substitute for doing the work entirely.

description:
If you want to use AI to help write your resume, start with these ChatGPT resume prompts. Just copy and paste, and be sure to edit the output as needed before submitting!

In this video, we’ll go over 4 main ways to use ChatGPT to write a high-quality resume:

1. Create a resume from scratch
2. Tailor your existing resume to better match specific job descriptions
3. Write effective resume bullet points
4. Craft resume summaries and professional summaries

You can use these ChatGPT resume prompts on Bard, too—and let us know which results you prefer!

How to do it:

1. Pull up the job description you’re interested in. (We recommend doing so in Teal’s free Job Tracker, which highlights the most important keywords from the job posting and saves you a step when you ask ChatGPT to create a tailored resume. It also saves you from having to toggle back and forth between multiple job boards!)

2. You can create your resume in a Word document, Google document, or resume builder tool. For the examples here, we’ll use Teal’s free Resume Builder.

3. Open ChatGPT in a third tab or window. In ChatGPT, copy and paste each of the following prompts, one at a time, followed by the job description where specified.

4. Take the responses that ChatGPT generates, copy them, and paste them back into your resume.

5. Though ChatGPT can provide suggestions, they’re not always 100% accurate. Edit as needed to make sure the metrics are correct and the tone and voice sound like you.

title: ChatGPT LinkedIn Tips: 4 Ways to Optimize Your Profile with AI
description:
ChatGPT  LinkedIn. 

If you're job searching, a strong LinkedIn profile can help you stand out to recruiters and hiring managers—and ChatGPT can help you put your best foot forward. 

Here's how: 

00:00 Introduction
00:10 What does "optimize your LinkedIn profile" mean?
00:37 LinkedIn "About" section
02:15 LinkedIn headline
03:26 "Experience" section 
04:58 LinkedIn messages
06:00 Wrap-up & conclusion

Step-by-step details on 4 ways to use ChatGPT to optimize your LinkedIn profile: 

1 Update your LinkedIn “About” section

– Prompt: "Write a LinkedIn About section using my resume." OR “Write a professional summary using my work experience and include my total years of experience, the keyword “X”, and keep it shorter than 150 words.”

– Type “Shift" + "Enter” to create a new line. 

– Copy the text from your resume (ideally from the Teal Resume Builder!) into ChatGPT below the prompt.

– Save your results in a separate document and click "Try Again" to regenerate as many versions as you need. 

– Tweak as needed and paste the summary back into the "About" section of your LinkedIn profile.

2  Optimize your LinkedIn headline

– Prompt: "Write a LinkedIn headline using my resume and keep it shorter than 220 characters.” OR “Write a LinkedIn headline in a conversational tone using my work experience and  the keywords “X” and “Y.” Keep it shorter than 220 characters.”

– Type “Shift" + "Enter” to create a new line. 

– Copy the text from your resume into ChatGPT below the prompt.

– Save your results in a separate document and click "Try Again" to regenerate as many versions as you need. 

– Tweak as needed and paste the headline into your LinkedIn profile.

3 Update your "Experience" section (aka your LinkedIn resume achievements)

– Prompt: "Write 3 resume achievements for [TITLE] and include success metrics using the keywords X, Y, and Z." (You can pull the keywords from the job description!)

– Type “Shift" + "Enter” to create a new line. 

– Copy the text from a job description into ChatGPT below the prompt.

– Save your results in a separate document (or your Teal Resume Builder!) and click "Try Again" to regenerate as many versions as you need. 

– Tweak as needed and paste into your LinkedIn "Experience" section. 

4 Write LinkedIn messages

– Prompt: "Write a LinkedIn message to thank the hiring manager for her time for the interview for the [TITLE] role at [COMPANY].” (Or use a similar prompt to check the status of your application!)

– Tweak as needed before sending. 

 Note: You'll want to edit these after AI takes the first pass. The tech is there to help and support you, but we don't encourage using it as a substitute for doing the work entirely.

title: How to Use ChatGPT to Write a Cover Letter (Is a ChatGPT Cover Letter Better?!)
description:
Want to use ChatGPT to write a cover letter? It's one of the BEST things you can outsource to AI in your job search—and it's easy to do. 

Here's how: 

1. Open up ChatGPT. For the prompt, you have a few options: 

– Write my cover letter for the [TITLE] role at [COMPANY] in a conversational tone, using my resume below as a reference. (Replace the title and company with options more relevant to your potential future role and company!)
– Write a cover letter with metrics for the following job description. Use my resume for reference, and keep it shorter than 400 words. 
– Write a cover letter for X role at X company and include the 5 most important keywords from the job description.

2.  Type “Shift” + “Enter” to create a new line. Paste your most recent resume, minus any personal contact information at the top. 

3. When you get your result, save it in a Google Doc or Word doc.

title: Do Years of Experience Matter?
description:
When it comes to job titles, you’d think think “years of experience” would be a simple objective thing right? Well, apparently not… I looked at over 300 jobs in the marketing career path and found that it was all over the map. Ideally, you could get a sense of the range of years required per job from the job title. The job titles are also all over the map. Companies use many variations to delineate the symbolic level. In marketing, the titles I found were: 

Marketing Coordinator
Senior Marketing Coordinator
Marketing Associate
Senior Marketing Associate
Assistant Marketing Manager
Marketing Manager
Senior Marketing Manager
Marketing Specialist
Associate Director, Marketing
Senior Marketing Lead
Marketing Lead
Head of Marketing
Vice President of Marketing

For a job seeker, the TL;DR is you need to search for more titles than the ones you think you’re qualified for. If you think your role should be Marketing Manager, also search for Marketing Lead and even Senior Marketing Manager. We’ve created a simple Google Sheet that will create all the variations for you and it also includes links to quickly run job searches. Below is a short YouTube video explaining how it works.

Dave here, CEO and founder of Teal.  I’m excited to share the features we've added to the Job Tracker and how we're continuing to iterate on and improve the tool. With all of these changes, we’re growing quickly! We have more than 14,000 users, 50,000 jobs saved, and half a million keywords extracted from jobs.

  The backstory

If you follow recommended best practices to land a job you love, you’re applying to 20-40 jobs a week! Most of the tools out there to manage this process are built for companies and not individuals. We wanted to level the playing field. Being in the job search vertical, we've seen the common pain points of a job search that most people experience multiple times in their career. So, we built a tool to solve these pain points and improve the job search process for our users.

 Our biggest change

The newest way we've leveled the playing field? We've made Teal's Job Tracker **100% free, forever.** Accessibility is important to us, and now everyone can use Teal's Job Tracker.

 How does Teal's Job Tracker improve your job search?

Let me walk you through our features and why we're the best tool to enable job seekers to more effectively search.

 Make job searching easier

Everyone has to do it at some point, but no one enjoys it. The Teal Job Tracker does the heavy lifting of organizing, tracking, and managing all the jobs in your pipeline. You can apply to jobs faster and land a great job sooner.

 Save roles from all the job boards to one place

Our Chrome extension allows you to instantly save jobs from all the major job boards straight to your Job Tracker dashboard so you can easily see all of the jobs you've saved. In the dashboard, you can organize the roles by your interest level, location, application status, and more.

 Beat the gate-keeping process

Everyone knows you need an optimized resume to get noticed. Job listings often have hundreds to even thousands of applications, which means including the best keywords is vital to getting your resume noticed. When you save a position in the Job Tracker, it analyzes the description and highlights the keywords/skills you should consider adding to your resume to make it to the top of the pile.

 Stay organized by tracking your contacts for your job search

After saving a job, you can keep all of your notes, contact information, and activity linked directly to that position. Stop missing out on opportunities by setting follow-up dates for each job you apply to. Lastly, track and visualize your progress through each stage of your job search with our checklists.

 What's new in Job Tracker 2.0?

We're introducing new features to improve the effectiveness of your job search.

- Teal is 100% free now: no more trials, paywalls, or subscriptions. Anyone can use our tools to help them land a job they love and grow in their career.
- We’ve done a complete UI overhaul: we’re continuing to iterate on our polished, simple interface.

So the words you use need to grab attention, fast.

 Words like “team player”, “fast learner”, and “detail-oriented” sound nice…
but they don’t prove your impact.

They show who you are as a person, not why you’re the best fit for the role.

And phrases like “assisted with” or “familiar with”?

They scream vague and forgettable.

 Instead, use power words that show real ownership and achievement:

Executed
Launched
Managed
Increased / Decreased
Coordinated
Implemented
Facilitated
Established
Consolidated
Piloted
Boosted
Generated X revenue / profits

title: Lie On Resume #resume
description:
The job market is a language game.

Let’s talk about your resume—specifically, job titles.

Sometimes, it feels like companies hand out titles like “Member Delight Director” or “Happiness Coordinator.” But at the end of the day, these are customer support roles.

Recruiters aren’t searching for “Happiness Coordinator” on LinkedIn. They’re searching for industry-standard terms.

Here’s my advice: normalize your titles.

On your resume, make them clear and recognizable to the hiring market. 

If you’re uneasy about this, you can always include the original title in parentheses:
 Customer Support Manager (Happiness Coordinator)

The bottom line is this: adapt to the market; don’t wait for the market to adapt to you.

And if you’re job hunting, tools like the Teal Resume Builder can help ensure your resume speaks the right language to get you noticed.

transcript: Do recruiters only read a resume for 7 seconds? Yeah, sometimes. But the reason is because it's pretty easy to eliminate a lot of resumes in that amount of time. Resumes that need to be read for more time are read for more time. Let me show you where my eyes go when I open a resume. Keeping in mind there is nothing more important than the experience on a resume. It has to match up with the job. When I open a resume like this with nothing but buzzwords and a long summary, I don't read it because I know there's nothing individualized in there. I go right down here to the experience. I can quickly get a feel for what this person was doing and this is aligned. If I'm looking for a software engineer, this person's out. I don't need to read it for more than 7 seconds. But I will dig in after this. You can also get me to keep reading by telling me immediately at the top what you need me to know and how it aligns with the job I'm looking for. Doing that combined with a summary that's very specific to you versus generic summary can do a lot. This is likely going to make me keep reading if I'm looking for a marketing director with demand gen experience. It's not about the order or the specific sections. It's about how quickly can I see what I need to see.

title: "Can you re-apply after getting rejected?"
transcript: Getting rejected for a job does not mean you can never work at that company. Unfortunately, we don't always get to know why we were rejected. Somebody else could have just applied earlier, breezed through the whole process, and then they only were hiring one role. That's not on you. Maybe the company did see a misalignment between what you were saying you were looking for and what they were offering, in which case I would hope they would actually let you know. And if it was something like maybe not enough experience, you're going to get more of that as you work more. Maybe you go somewhere else for a year or two. If that company relists that position, it's absolutely worth applying.

description:

When it comes to timing, the thing to be aware of is if you are applying after it’s been open for a while there might be someone who is the company like who is just further along in the process. That doesn’t mean you aren’t qualified or the company won’t look at your application, but it might mean they have already found someone who move forward with. #jobapplication #jobapplicationtips #jobapplications #application #jobseeker #jobseekertips

title: Should You Have THIS In Your LinkedIn Headline? ✍️
description:
Lots of people put "Ex-[COMPANY]" in their headline—but should you?

Some would argue yes, that your headline is what gets people to click—the trailer for your profile.

But would you start a first date by talking about your ex?

Maybe you worked for a big-name company—that's awesome. But that's what your "Experience" section is for. Or your "About" section.

Your LinkedIn headline only has 220 characters, so those are better spent showing your value and keywords, not summarizing the places you've worked.

title: How to Change Your "Open to Work" Setting on LinkedIn So It's Open to Recruiters Only
description:
You can change your "open to work" setting to show so that it's open to recruiters only. That way, you don't get the green banner around your profile photo on LinkedIn, but you still show up in LinkedIn Recruiter as a filter that people can search by. Here's how to change that setting right in your LinkedIn profile. 

1. You're going to go over to your profile and click the "Open To" button. They recently updated this. It used to be in your settings. 
2. Now you're gonna go over to "Finding a New Job." You can change any of these settings. There's a cool thing where you can add titles you want to be available for.
3. Show that you're open to recruiters only, which will keep LinkedIn from showing the green banner.

title: How to Turn on LinkedIn Creator Mode
description:
If you see a LinkedIn profile that has hashtags below the headline, that means that that person's turned on LinkedIn Creator Mode. It's a setting for members who regularly create content on the platform, and you can choose up to five topics that you want to talk about. If you have Creator Mode turned on, the call to action button will show up as "Follow" instead of "Connect."

Here's how to turn it on. On the top, right. Go to the "Me" section and then "View Profile." Scroll down until you see creator mode there you can type in up to five topics that you want to talk about regularly. 

Some creators will also have the option to see additional tools, such as LinkedIn Live or newsletter creation.

#linkedin #linkedintips #jobsearch #careeradvice #career

title: Is the Open to Work Setting on LinkedIn Desperate?
description:
There's a lot of talk lately about whether or not it's desperate for job seekers to use the green "Open to Work" banner on LinkedIn.  Should you use the #OpenToWork banner? YES! It helps hiring managers & recruiters source talent and makes it clear you’re willing to have a conversation. Hiring is a long process, and convincing someone who’s happy at their job to leave is really hard—so this saves time for both parties. (Note: If you’re concerned about anyone knowing you’re looking, be careful with this setting. We can post a part 2 about how to choose who views your "open to work" settings.)

#linkedin #career #careeradvice #jobsearch #linkedintips #opentowork #jobapplication

title: Customizing your LinkedIn URL
description:
Creating a custom LinkedIn is easy to do, looks cleaner on your resume, and makes your LinkedIn profile stand out (and it's easier to remember, too!). 

Here's how to do it: 

1. Use our free Teal Chrome extension's LinkedIn Review tool and click the "edit now" button at the bottom.  
2. That will take you to the part of LinkedIn where you can customize your public settings. We suggest using your full name in some capacity, whether you add in a dash or a number to differentiate yourself. 
3. You'll also want to make sure that your custom LinkedIn URL is included on your resume, so copy/paste it from LinkedIn, head over to our free resume builder, and paste your link.
